NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI computing value chain as a fabless semiconductor designer, critically dependent upstream on TSMC for cutting-edge chip fabrication and SK Hynix for HBM memory, while commanding exceptional pricing power downstream with hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) who collectively account for the majority of its explosive data center revenue growth. Its near-monopoly position in AI GPU compute (estimated 80%+ market share in AI accelerators) makes it both a critical supplier to and a key beneficiary of the global AI infrastructure buildout.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly sophisticated consumer electronics supply chain, acting as a powerful orchestrator that designs its own silicon and software while outsourcing manufacturing to a concentrated network of Asian suppliers — most critically TSMC for chip fabrication and Samsung/LG for displays. On the downstream side, Apple sells primarily through its own direct channels (Apple Stores, apple.com) and carrier/retail partners, while its high-margin Services segment increasingly monetizes its 2B+ active device installed base through licensing deals, the App Store, and platform fees.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits at the heart of the global memory supply chain as one of only three major DRAM producers and one of a handful of NAND manufacturers, making it critically dependent on a small group of highly specialized semiconductor equipment suppliers — particularly ASML, Applied Materials, and Lam Research — for its capital-intensive fab operations. On the demand side, Micron's revenue is increasingly driven by AI infrastructure buildout, with hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google) and GPU leaders like NVIDIA representing the fastest-growing and highest-margin customer segments, particularly for HBM and high-capacity server DRAM.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM Holdings sits at the apex of the global semiconductor IP ecosystem, licensing its CPU, GPU, and system IP architectures to virtually every major chip designer worldwide rather than manufacturing silicon itself, making its upstream dependencies primarily EDA software vendors and cloud infrastructure providers. Its downstream relationships span the entire semiconductor value chain — from mobile SoC designers like Qualcomm and Apple to hyperscale cloud providers building custom silicon on ARM architectures — giving it unparalleled leverage but also concentration risk among a relatively small number of high-volume licensees.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology sits at a critical mid-tier position in the data infrastructure semiconductor supply chain, heavily dependent on TSMC for advanced node fabrication and ARM for processor IP while designing custom ASICs and merchant silicon for hyperscale cloud providers, networking OEMs, and storage vendors. Its growing custom silicon business for AWS, Google, and Microsoft has shifted its downstream mix toward a concentrated set of high-value hyperscaler relationships, making cloud capex cycles a primary demand driver.
